Helpdesk ticket #8876: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- no server farm, no other pod, and name
lookups time out too. It can still ping its gateway address 10.1.1.1.
host_2_1_1_1 is unaffected and reaches everything normally. Diagnose
host_1_1_1_1's connectivity.

injection.action: point the host's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.1.1.254

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default gateway / default route points at wrong address (10.1.1.254 instead of 10.1.1.1)
bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The IPv4 default route (gateway configuration) on `host_1_1_1_1`.

**Mechanism:** `host_1_1_1_1`'s routing table has `default via 10.1.1.254 dev eth0`. No device on the 10.1.1.0/24 segment holds the IP 10.1.1.254 — the real access-side gateway router (`switch_dist_1_1` / `router_core_1`) sits at `10.1.1.1`. When the host forwards any packet destined outside its local subnet, the kernel looks up the default route, attempts to ARP-resolve 10.1.1.254, receives no reply, and immediately returns an ICMP "Destination Host Unreachable" message to itself. This explains every reported symptom: cross-pod ICMP to `host_2_1_1_1` (10.2.1.2) fails, pings to web servers and the DNS server (10.200.0.x) fail, and DNS queries never leave the host — all off-subnet traffic is black-holed at the ARP stage. The user's observation that 10.1.1.1 remains pingable is consistent: that address is within the directly connected 10.1.1.0/24 subnet, so the kernel routes it via the link-local entry without consulting the default gateway. `host_2_1_1_1` is unaffected because it carries the correct gateway `10.2.1.1`.

**Localization:** `host_1_1_1_1`, `eth0`, default route entry.

**Root cause:** The default gateway on `host_1_1_1_1` is set to the non-existent address `10.1.1.254` instead of the correct `10.1.1.1`.

**Fix:** Replace the default route — `ip route del default && ip route add default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0` — and persist the correct gateway in the host's startup configuration.
